named_subject: a pig seen from the side, with a spiral snout, two pointed ears, a round body and short stick legs
action: The pig stands still facing left for the first six frames, then its body swells and grows larger in the frame as if coming closer, while it stays in side view.
identity_gap: Frames 1-6 match the doodle closely, but from frame 13 on the ears tip over into a sideways zigzag, the back of the head becomes one long diagonal line, and the front legs separate from the body, so the late frames drift away from the doodle's construction.
notes: In the film the pig turns from a side view to face the camera and walks toward it, but the drawing never turns; it only scales up, and it jumps in position at frame 9 (shifts right and shrinks) and frame 13 (shifts left and grows). The change that would help most is to animate the head and body turning toward the viewer with steady in-between positions instead of rescaling the side-view drawing in jumps.
